We use the term character to refer to the social category (men or women) into which one is categorized—either by others or by oneself.

Essentialism refers to the belief that group membership is biologically determined and stable (throughout history and throughout group members’ lives) and that group members share an underlying “essence” that makes them similar to one another and different from other groups ( Rhodes & Gelman, 2009 ).
